readerTitle: The tire return that became free advertising
caseNote: 실제 기업 일화 (Nordstrom 타이어 반품) + 실제 기업 (L.L.Bean 반품 정책 변경) + 가상 사례 (생활용품 매장, 상업용 청소 회사)
insight: 서비스는 판매 뒤에 드는 비용이 아니라, 고객이 다른 사람에게 전하는 이야기를 만드는 마케팅이다.
misconception: 마케팅은 고객을 데려오고, 서비스는 판매 뒤에 최대한 줄여야 할 비용이다.

sources.text: Spector, R. & McCarthy, P. (1995). The Nordstrom Way. Wiley. (타이어 반품 일화, 직원 안내 카드)
L.L.Bean, customer letter on changes to its satisfaction guarantee (February 2018)

factChecks.note: Nordstrom 타이어 일화는 1970년대 알래스카에서 타이어를 팔던 매장을 Nordstrom이 인수한 뒤 생긴 일로 전해집니다. 세부 내용(연도, 도시, 금액)은 자료마다 다르고 각색되었을 수 있어 카드에는 일화로만 표시하고 금액과 연도는 쓰지 않았습니다.
Nordstrom 직원 안내 카드 문구 "Use good judgment in all situations"는 널리 인용되지만 실제 사용 시기와 형태를 확인하세요. 카드에는 "reportedly"로 적었습니다.
L.L.Bean은 2018년 2월 기한 없는 만족 보증을 구매 후 1년(영수증 필요)으로 바꾸고, 중고 거래로 산 물건 반품 등 남용을 이유로 들었습니다. 게시 전 원문 서신으로 다시 확인하세요.
생활용품 매장과 청소 회사 사례는 모두 설명용 가상 사례이며 수치($60 등)도 가상입니다.

cards.title: The tire return that became free advertising
body: A department store that sells clothes and shoes does not sell tires. Yet in a story told about Nordstrom for decades, a customer walked in with a set of tires and got his money back.
It probably cost the store a few hundred dollars. The story has been repeated in books, classrooms and newspapers ever since.

image.label: A clerk at a fashion counter accepting a stack of car tires
image.brief: 따뜻한 일러스트. 고급 의류 매장 계산대에 자동차 타이어 네 개가 쌓여 있고, 직원이 웃으며 환불해 주는 장면. 뒤편 손님들이 놀란 표정으로 휴대폰을 꺼냄. 실제 매장 로고나 간판은 쓰지 않음.

cards.title: A return outside the policy.
body: You run a homewares store. Your return policy is 90 days. A regular customer brings back a $60 lamp she bought 14 months ago. The switch has failed.
Your staff member asks you what to do. What do you tell her?

options.text: Say no politely. The policy is 90 days, and rules are rules
options.feedback: You save $60 and keep the policy clean. But a loyal customer leaves with a story about being turned away, and she will tell it.

options.text: Refund her in full this time. It's only $60
options.feedback: You win this customer back. But next time your staff will have to ask again, and customers will get different answers on different days.

options.text: Refund her, and let staff fix problems like this up to a set amount without asking
options.feedback: It costs a little more over a year. In return, every staff member can create the kind of moment customers repeat to friends.

cards.title: The cheapest ad Nordstrom never bought.
body: The tire story is an anecdote, and it may be embellished. One version says the store had once been a tire shop before Nordstrom bought it.
What matters is what it did. Nordstrom never had to pay for it to spread. Customers, journalists and teachers retold it because it was surprising.
No ad saying "we care about you" travels that far. A strange, true-sounding act of service does.

cards.title: Service as marketing
body: **Service as marketing** means every service moment is also a message: to the customer, and to everyone that customer talks to.
Ads make promises. Service is the proof people actually see. When the two match, customers become your messengers. When service breaks the promise, they spread that too.

image.label: One service moment rippling out to many people
image.brief: 가운데 직원과 고객 한 명이 대화하는 작은 장면. 그 주변으로 물결처럼 원이 퍼지고, 원마다 친구, 동료, 가족이 말풍선으로 이야기를 전하는 모습. 깔끔한 플랫 인포그래픽 스타일.

cards.title: Why service travels further than ads.
body: Nordstrom reportedly gave new staff a card with one main rule: use good judgment in all situations. The point was to let people on the floor solve problems on the spot.
list: **Stories need surprise:** people repeat what goes beyond what they expected
**Friends are believed:** a story from someone you know beats a claim from the company
**Problems are the stage:** a fixed mistake is more memorable than a smooth day
cards.callout: Your service budget is part of your marketing budget, whether you count it that way or not.
cards.softwareNote: In software, a support reply that fixes a problem in minutes, or a founder who answers a bug report personally, often ends up in a public post or a review. Those posts can bring in more sign-ups than paid ads.

cards.title: In B2B, service is the sales pitch.
body: Business buyers rarely trust a brochure. Before signing, they call peers and ask, "How are they when things go wrong?"

That answer comes from your service team, not your sales team. The account manager who returns calls, the engineer who stays late, the clear invoice: each becomes the reference that wins the next client.
In businesses with few, large customers, one good or bad service story can reach every buyer in the industry.

cards.title: Generosity has to be sustainable.
body: L.L.Bean was famous for taking back almost anything, at any time. In 2018 it limited returns to one year with proof of purchase, saying some people were abusing the promise, for example returning worn-out items bought second-hand.
Service as marketing works when the cost is bounded and the product is solid. Service cannot hide a bad product for long. And a generous promise you later take back can become its own story.

cards.title: Now it's a commercial cleaning company.
body: You clean offices for 40 business clients. At 7 p.m., the office manager of a well-known client emails: a pipe leaked, and the CEO hosts investors at 8 a.m. Your crew normally arrives at 6 a.m.

options.text: Stick to the contract. The crew arrives at 6 a.m. as usual
options.feedback: You avoid extra cost, but the client may face investors in a wet office. The story the office manager tells will be about you.

options.text: Send a crew tonight and bill the standard overtime rate
options.feedback: Fair, and the problem gets solved. The story is "they fixed it, for a fee", which is good but not one people retell.

options.text: Send a crew tonight at no charge this once, and say why
options.feedback: It costs one evening of wages. In return, the office manager has a story to tell her CEO and her peers, which is exactly how B2B referrals start.

cards.title: Every service moment is an ad your customers write.
body: Treat service decisions as marketing decisions: ask what story each one will create.
**Try it today:** think of the last problem a customer brought you. Write down the story they would tell a friend about how you handled it.
